verdicts.claim: SQLite enables an automatic checkpoint by default. It fires when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB at 4 KiB
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'WAL file accumulates about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; 'occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added a NOOP checkpoint mode: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(NOOP) and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP
verdicts.evidence: 3.51.0 release log: 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2().'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA journal_size_limit=N (default -1, no limit) truncates a larger WAL file to N bytes each time the WAL resets
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets ... it is truncated to the limit'; 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).'

verdicts.claim: SQLite developer Dan found it on 2026-03-03. It is likely present in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). Version 3.51.3
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed'; '3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09)... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.'

verdicts.claim: Antithesis (2026-08-12) found it in 15 minutes on 3.51.2 with a generic workload of concurrent WAL writes and checkpoints; the same run
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; 'repeated the exercise with 3.51.3 ... the run came back green.'

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton (2026-08-23) wrote a 100-line C program ... mmap_size 1 GB, about 65,536 rows of 3,900-byte blobs ... lost writes in about 3.5 to 4.3
verdicts.evidence: Post: 'About 100 lines of C'; mmap_size=1073741824; i<65536; randomblob(3900); 'real 0m4.286s' / 'real 0m3.454s'; ATTEMPTS default 200; 3.53.0 'you'll stop seeing these lost writes'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale's control plane has used SQLite as its primary database since 2022 ... 19 corruption incidents over about six months, starting in Au
verdicts.evidence: Register: 'primary database since 2022'; 'snapshot ... every few minutes ... S3'; 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption'. Techzine: 'nineteen instances of database corruption over the course of half a year'; 'Two months later, that exact situation was detected, without the database becoming corrupted.'

verdicts.claim: According to Techzine, SQLite 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) shipped the WAL-reset fix first. SQLite withdrew 3.52.0 ... features moved to 3.53.0 (2026-04-0
verdicts.evidence: 3.52.0 page: 'On 2026-03-06 Withdrawn. All of the features ... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; 3.53.0: 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'; Techzine: 'The fix was initially included in SQLite 3.52.0 ... rounding of certain floating-point conversions'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.3 logged the reason 'wal overwritten by another process' ... Litestream therefore recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0 on h
verdicts.evidence: Tips: 'Disable autocheckpoints for high write load servers' ... 'PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0;' and 'PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;'; issue #547 log: reason="wal overwritten by another process"

verdicts.claim: In February 2026 Syncthing kept SQLite auto-checkpoint enabled and added a timer-based checkpointer ... hours-long transactions pinned W
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing forum: 'We don't disable the auto checkpoint functionality'; 'If a transaction is open for hours'; 'replace the timer based checkpointer and move the logic into our connection pool'; 'WAL reaches critical levels of multiple gigabytes ... exclusive locking'

notes: All 10 claims verified from the local source cache; 0 web fetches used.
